text:
ashley_ml: Quick heads-up — I ran end-to-end burst sims for the Dedicated pool shapes (8x A100, 12x A10x, 16x A10x) across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Wanted a sanity-check on headroom assumptions before we update the runbook.
pranav_eng: nice. what's the baseline QPS and target p95 we're sizing for?
maria_ops: FYI storage/job startup didn't dominate in earlier runs, but network egress bumped p95 in eu-west-1 during the 2x burst.
ashley_ml: baseline is 800 qps steady, simulate 3x burst to 2400 sustained for 30s, then 6x short spike to 4800 for 8s. target p95 <= 250ms for interactive gen path, 95th tokens/sec SLA for batch is looser.
devon_sre: can you paste the sim command? want to re-run with our noise model.
ashley_ml: sure —
```
# sim invocation
python infra/burst_sim.py \
  --region us-west-2,eu-west-1 \
  --gpu-shapes A100:8,A10x:12,A10x:16 \
  --steady-qps 800 \
  --burst-multipliers 3,6 \
  --burst-durations 30,8 \
  --noise-model noise/vpc-egress.json \
  --metrics p50,p95,throughput
```
bench-bot: results uploaded: https://internal/bench/reports/1788882460 — summary posted below.
bench-bot: us-west-2 | 8x A100 | steady 800 -> p95=120ms, burst-3x p95=210ms, burst-6x p95=420ms (queueing observed). throughput cap ~9.6k tokens/s.
bench-bot: eu-west-1 | 8x A100 | steady 800 -> p95=135ms, burst-3x p95=245ms, burst-6x p95=480ms (network tail + kernel fallback spikes).
bench-bot: 12x A10x | us-west-2 | steady p95=160ms, 3x=280ms, 6x=520ms. 16x A10x improves steady but adds variance under burst due to packing overhead.
pranav_eng: interesting — A100 wins latency under bursts (less kernel fallback), but capacity per GPU vs cost matters. what concurrency per-GPU did you model?
ashley_ml: we used concurrency=8 for A100, concurrency=10 for A10x (observed optimal in local perf grid).
maria_ops: given those p95s, what's the recommended autoscale headroom? currently autoscale adds +40% capacity on warmup and +100% for emergency.
devon_sre: those defaults were conservative. for a 3x burst target we can set warmup headroom to +50% and emergency to +120% for eu-west-1 given network variance. us-west-2 could be +40% warmup, +100% emergency.
pranav_eng: propose we encode region-specific policies: europe gets wider buffer because of observed network noise. Also add a kernel-prewarm step for A10x to reduce fallback churn (preload common kernels).
maria_ops: agree. also add a gradual ramp policy: when scaling from steady->burst, do 40% scale immediately then 60% over 5s to avoid sudden queue storms.
ashley_ml: can we quantify runway? with current numbers, an 8x A100 pool sized for steady 800 qps handles 3x burst for ~45s before p95 crosses 400ms threshold. 12x A10x at same commit hits degraded p95 sooner (~25s).
pranav_eng: that's helpful. we should add a recommended pool change: for customers who expect >3x sustained bursts, prefer A100 pools with concurrency tuned to 6-8 and set warmup headroom +60%.
devon_sre: note — A100 costs ~1.8x per hour vs A10x in our procurement. include a cost/run tradeoff in the runbook with a simple calc.
ashley_ml: added a calc in the report: cost-per-peak-token = (pool-hour-cost * burst-duration)/(tokens-served). example attached.
autoscale-bot: /note Updated autoscale-policy draft: regionOverrides { eu-west-1: { warmupHeadroom:0.6, emergencyHeadroom:1.2, rampSeconds:5 }, us-west-2: { warmupHeadroom:0.4, emergencyHeadroom:1.0, rampSeconds:5 } }
pranav_eng: next steps: 1) pranav to vet kernel-prewarm patch 2) devon to update runbook with region overrides and cost calc 3) ashley to re-run sims with added prewarm and new concurrency table.
maria_ops: tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:
ashley_ml: I'll re-run tomorrow with prewarm and post new report. thanks all. :thumbsup:
